Md. Abdul Wadudd Bhuiyan along with Mr. Ahasanul Quayyum, Advocate ------ For the Plaintiff-Petitioner 
Mr. Moin uddin along with Mr. Mosharaf Hossain Sarder, Advocates ------ For the defendant opposite party No.1
parties:
Wali Ahmed ------ Plaintiff-Petitioner
Versus
Monjur Kader and another ------ Defendant-Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. S.H. Md. Nurul Huda Jaigidar, J:-On an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the plaintiff-petitioner, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.06.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.181 of 2006, should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of this Rule, are that, the petitioner as plaintiff instituted filed Title Suit No.81 of 1992 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge Dhaka for restoration of possession in the suit land under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 against the opposite parties as defendants. On being transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka, it was renumbered as Title Suit No.326 of 1997 and thereafter again renumbered as Title Suit No.181 of 2006. The suit was dismissed on contest by th6 impugned judgment and decree dated 24.06.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka and the instant revision has been preferred. 

3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner, in short, is that professor Nurun Nahar Ahmed, on 01.11.1982, by two registered sale deeds sold .1650 decimals of land to the plaintiff petitioner and handed over the possession of the land. After purchase, the petitioner mutated his name in the Revenue Office and paid rents of the purchased land. The plaintiff-petitioner, while was enjoying right, title and interest of his purchased land, cultivated bore paddy through borgadar. He developed the land by earth filing at the cost of 3 lac taka and bounded by bamboo pillar, bamboo fencing and erected one kacha room with bamboo posts, bamboo fencing and tin roof. He appointed one care taker who used to this reside therein and look after the land. In this way the plaintiff petitioner had been peacefully possessing his purchased suit land. 

4. On the night following 03.11.1991 at about 03.00 .m.; defendant opposite party Nos.1 and 2 with some other hired gunda armed with deadly weapons by force dispossessed the plaintiff-petitioner 's caretaker and his other 2 friends, who had been staying in the tin shed room and boundary fencing made by the plaintiff-petitioner. The care taker and his two friends went to the residence of the plaintiff-petitioner and informed about the occurrence. In this way, the plaintiff-petitioner was dispossessed from the suit land by the defendant opposite parties with help of hired `gundas'. As such, the plaintiff-petitioner instituted the suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 for recovery of possession in the suit land on 29.04.1992. 

5. The defendant opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement and denied all allegations made in the plaint and thereby denied the alleged possession in and dispossession from the suit land. According to the case of the defendant, the plaintiff was not in possession of the disputed land and that the defendants (opposite parties) have been long and that the question of alleged dispossession by the opposite parties did not arise at all. 

6. Trial Court on consideration of the evidence, oral and documentary arrived at a decision that the plaintiff-petitioner could not prove his case of possession and dispossession and as such, dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment. 

7. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff preferred this revisional application and obtained the Rule. 

8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan with Mr. Ahasanul Quayyum, the learned Advocates have appeared on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner. By filing an affidavit in reply to the counter affidavit of the defendant opposite parties. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan submits that on 04.11.1991 at night the defendants forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff-petitioner from the suit land and since then they have been illegally occupying the suit land. Learned Advocate contends that the plaintiff petitioner has been able to prove his case by adducing substantive evidence and that the defendants could not prove their possession in the suit land prior to the date of dispossession. It is submitted that the defendants also filed Title Suit No.208 of 2006 against the plaintiff-petitioner for permanent injunction in respect of land measuring 1650 out of their 36 decimals purchased from same suit Plot No.203, boundary area of which was given showing defendants, private road in C.S. Plot No.203 on the north, road on the south; defendants under construction buildings on the west in the C.S. Plot No.203, and own land of defendants in C.S. Plot No.203 on the east, where they had garments factory and to the extreme east west built pucca boundary wall with heavy R.C.C. pillars. The said soil for permanent injunction being No.128 of 1992, was ultimately renumbered Title Suit No.208 of 2006 in the Court of Assistant Judge and the suit was decreed in favour of these defendants, but the suit land measuring 161/2 decimals of the present suit of the plaintiff is not identical and same with the suit land of the defendants in the said suit for permanent injunction, rather both are of separate entity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff petitioner Wali Ahmed filed Title Suit No.81 of 1992 renumbered as Title Suit No.181 of 2006 giving a separate schedule in the plaint measuring 16lA decimals out of the same big plot which is butted and bounded on the north road and Md. Dulal Miah, on the south; Ballot, on the east; Abdus Sattar, on the west; formerly Md. Mafizur Rahman, at present Fatema Besunia; and this portion of land is located to the east of the land of Fatema Basunia, and to the further west of Fatema Basunia, claimed land of the defendants is situated, which was made suit land of permanent injunction suit. Accordingly, the suit land of the petitioner is distinct and different showing marked distance from the suit land of Refatul Islam Chowdhury, plaintiff in Title Suit No.208 of 2006 (defendant in the present suit), but with ill motive, defendant Refatul Islam Chowdhury has tried to show plaintiffs suit land is within their 36 - decimals of land, which is not true. That the decree of permanent injunction was obtained by the defendant opposite parties in respect of their purchased land, where the plaintiff has not interest and the defendant opposite parties do not also claim on the plaintiffs earlier purchased 16l/2 decimals land with separate boundary demarcation. The learned Advocate has further pointed that in the judgment passed in defendant's Title Suit No.208 of 2006 for permanent injunction, the trial Court observed as follows: “অত্র মামমলার বাদী পক্ষ জাহের আলী ও আশেয়া বেগম কোন জমি দাবী করেন না। সেই সাথে বিবাদী পক্ষ সাল্লাবী বিবি, রোকেয়া বেগম ও ইছাকের ওয়ারিশ কাজেম আলী গং এর নিকট হইতে কোন সম্পত্তি দাবি করেন না। মালিকানা দাবীর ক্ষেত্রে কোন পক্ষেরই কোন পক্ষের সাথে স্বত্ত্বে কোন দ্বন্দ নাই।” It is also observed by the trial “বাদীর অত্র মামলার আরজিতে বর্ণিত চৌহদ্দি, বিবাদীর দেওয়ানী ১৮১/০৬ নং মামলার আরজিতে বর্ণিত চৌহদ্দির সাথে কোন মিল খুজিয়া পাওয়া যায় না।” PW.I in Title Suit No.208 of 2006 for permanent injunction as referred to by the trial in the impugned judgment, stated in his deposition “বিবাদীর জমির চৌহদ্দি ও আমাদের জমির চৌহদ্দি আলাদা” and in the plaint of title Suit No.208 of 2006 filed by the opposite parties it has been stated clearly that the suit property (.1650 decimals) of their suit is situated in the middle of 36 decimals of land which they purchased by different deed. 

9. With reference to the aforesaid admission about the fact that the plaintiffs suit land and defendants disputed land of their respective suits are not same, the learned Advocate submits that the decree of the 'permanent injunction suit does not in any way affect the plaintiffs claim of possession and subsequent dispossession, which is the subject matter to been seen in Title Suit No.181 of 2006 filed by the plaintiff petitioner. The learned Advocate further submits that just after the occurrence of dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land he lodged General Diary Entry No.191 dated 04.11.1991 with Mohammadpur Police Station and immediately thereafter, plaintiff also filed a complaint case against the defendant for criminal offences of the defendants for selfsame occurrence of dispossession, which is still pending. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the written statement filed in Title Suit No.208 of 2006 (suit for permanent injunction) which reads as follows: 

"(f) That on 04.11.1991 the plaintiff and another person Manjur Quader along with many `mastan' people forcibly destroyed the surrounding bamboo fencing and liner ghar' of the defendant and trespassed into the defendants land measuring .1650 decimals, the plaintiff and other person Manjur Quader trespassing into the defendans land has been occupying the some illegally and forcibly. They are mere tress passers only. They have no right, title and interest in the said land which is the suit land. 

"(g) That the defendant filed Title Suit No.181 of 1992 under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, in the Court of Sub Judge, Dhaka for recovery of possession of defendants .1650 decimals of land, which is suit land. The said suit is pending for adjudication. The defendant also filed Complaint Case No. 1287a-1/91 under Sections 448/427f380 Penal Code in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for the criminal activity of the plaintiff in the manner stated above, "These facts and circumstances speak volume of the true story of plaintiffs earlier possession and dispossession, he added. He submits that since the defendant did not get decree in respect of the same property of the plaintiff, no appeal was necessary to be preferred. 

10. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court in his judgment, misread misinterpreted the pleadings of the parties and evidence available on record which needs interference by this Court, and since the plaintiff has been able to prove his case, the instant rule may be made absolute by setting aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

11. Mr. Moinuddin with Mosharrof Hossain Sarder, the learned Advocates, have appeared on behalf of the opposite parties and a counter affidavit in reply has also been tiled, Mr. Moinuddin submits that the defendant opposite parties have been owning and possessing the suit property and they have substantial interest in the suit property, whereas the plaintiff petitioner had/has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and that the plaintiff petitioners witnesses made self-contradictory testimony and as such their evidence are not reliable. It is submitted that the trial Court on proper assessment of evidence, oral and documentary arrived at a correct decision and dismissed the suit in the right direction. That the trial Court rightly held that the plaintiff petitioner could not prove his case of possession in and dispossession from the suit property and committed no error of law resulting in an enor in the decision occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the suit and as such there is no cogent reason to interfere with the correct, valid and tenable judgment of the trial Court. The learned Advocate further submits that the present opposite party No.2 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.128 of 1992 (subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.208 of 2006) before the Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka against the present petitioner as the sole defendant for same suit land; the present petitioner as defendant contested the suit by filing written statement and the Title Suit No.181 of 2006 filed by the present petitioner against plaintiff Title Suit No.208 of 2006 were simultaneously heard one after another and the trial Court dismissed the Title Suit No.181 of 2006 filed by the present petitioner and decreed Title Suit No.208 of 2006 filed by the present opposite party No.2 for permanent injunction as the present petitioner as plaintiff of Title Suit No.181 of 2006 could not prove his case of alleged possession and dispossession. The decree of title Suit No.208 of 2006 (permanent injunction) in respect of the same suit property still valid and the plaintiff petitioner did not even prefer any appeal against the decree of the permanent injunction. Now the plaintiff cannot get any relief in this revisional application. There is no ground in the revisional application calling for interference with the impugned judgment. 

12. The provision of Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 reads as follows: 

"9. Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property -If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit *** recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. 

Nothing in this Section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to recover possession thereof. 

No suit under this Section shall be brought against (the government) 

No appeal shall lie from any order or decree passed in any suit instituted under this section, nor shall any review of any such orders or decree be allowed:' 

13. Thus in a suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 it is only necessary to prove whether the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land and he was dispossessed by the defendant and to see whether the plaintiff has filed the suit within 6(six) months from the date of dispossession and, if these facts are proved, the plaintiff can get his possession restored. There is no necessity to adjudicate the title of the parties in this nature of suit. 

14. The plaintiffs specific case is that, he was in possession of the schedule land of the plaint on the basis of registered purchase deeds dated 01.12.82 (Exts.5, 5(ka) and erected a but and bamboo fencing there upon. He got his name mutated in the khatian and has been paying rents. But the plaintiff was evicted by the defendants, on 04.11.1991 at 03.00 a.m. illegally by applying force. The onus obviously is upon the plaintiff to prove that he was in possession of the suit land up to 03.11.1991 and on 04.11.1991 at 03.00 am., he was dispossessed by the defendants otherwise than due C011170 of law. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the basis of his finding that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case disbelieving evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses. The learned Advocate for the petitioner persuaded us to go through the evidence of the parties in details and tried to show instances of misreading and non-consideration of the evidence by the trial Court. 

15. The plaintiff examined five witnesses including himself, as PW.I. PW.I Wali Ahmed in his examination in chief stated “আমি নালিশী ভূমিতে পূর্বে দখলে ছিলাম। নালিশী ভূমি থেকে ০৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে ১নং বিবাদী মঞ্জুর কাদের ২নং বিবাদী রেফায়েতুল ইসলাম আমাকে বেদখল করে। ফলে বাধ্য হয়ে আমি মামলা করিয়াছি। আমি দখল পুনরুদ্ধার চাই।” PW. I in his cross examination said “সত্য নহে ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে বিবাদীরা আমাকে বেদখল করে নাই। সত্য নহে নালিশী ভূমিতে মাটি ভরাট করি নাই বা টিনের ঘর করি নাই। ৪/১১/৯১ বেদখল হই। এই সময়ে কেয়ারটেকার ছিল।”  PW.2 Md. Hafiz Uddin who was staying in the suit but with caretaker of the plaintiff on the night of dispossession stated in his examination-in-chief “নালিশী সম্পত্তির ১৯৯১ সনের নভেম্বর মাসের ৩ তারিখে বিদাগত রাত্রে আমার নালিশী সম্পত্তির ঞরে ছিলাম। আমি আবুল খায়ের ও নাজিমুদ্দিন ছিলাম। রাত্রি ৩ টার দিকে ঘুমানো থাকাবস্থায় দরজা ধাক্কায় আমাদের ঘুম ভাংগিয়া যায়। আমরা চৌকির উপর বসি আমরা দরজার দিকে যাই। নাজিম উদ্দিন দরজা খুলে, হাবিব নামে এক লোক তাহার সাতে অপর লোক ঘরে ঢুকে ও নাজিম উদ্দিনের সার্টের কলার ধরে ও আমাদেরকে ধাক্কা দিয়া বের করে দেয়। আমরা বের হয়ে দেখি মঞ্জুর কাদের, কেফায়েতুল, তরুণ কুমার এবং এদের পিছনে ৭০/৮০ জন লোক মঞ্জুর কাদেরের হাতে শাবল ছিল। অন্যান্যদের হাতে লাঠি, শাব, দা অন্যান্য জিনিসপত্র ছিল। আমরা পূর্ব দিকে ৫০/৬০ হাত ধুরে আশ্রয় নেই। ওখান থেকে দেখি যে বাউন্ডারী, ঘর সবকিছু ভেঙ্গে নিয়া যায় ও নাঃ জায়গা খালি থাকে।”

PW.3 Nizam Uddin who was caretaker of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land stated in his examination-in-chief 

“নাঃ জমি নীচা ছিল বাদী মাটি ভরাট করেছে ১৯৯১ সনে জানুয়ারী- মার্চ পরযন্ত। বাদী একটা ঘর নির্মাণ বরে। বেড়া মুলি বাশের উপরে টিন। ১০ হাত চওড়া। ১৫ হাত লম্বা। আমি রাত্রে ঐ ঘরের কেয়ারটেকার হিসাবে থাকতাম, আবুল খায়ের, হাফিজ উদ্দিন মাঝে মাঝে এসে থাকতো। ১৯৯১ সনের নভেম্বর মাসের ৩ তারিখ রাত্রি ৩ টায় ঘটনা ঘটে। আমার সাথে আবুল খায়ের ও হাফিজ উদ্দিন ছিল। নালিশী জমির চারিদিকে মুলি বাশের বেড়া, বাশের খুটির বেড়া ছিল, গেট ছিল। রাত্রি তিনটায় দরজায় ধাক্কার শব্দ শুনে ঘুম ভেঙ্গে যায়। হাবিব আমাদেরকে বের হতে বলে আমরা বের হই নাই বাহির থেকে বলে জোর করে বের করে দাও। আমাদেরকে প্রানে মারার হুমকি দিলে আমরা বের হই।” He deposed that the defendants and their men took possession by force removing the structure and fencing of the plaintiff. PW.4 Md. Abut Khair stated in his examination-in-chief “১৯৯১/৩রা নভেম্বর আমি ও হাফিজ উদ্দিন নালিশী জমিতে উপরস্ত ঘরে যাই। আমরা ঐ ঘরে ঘুমাই। রাত্রি ৩টার দিকে জোরে জোরে শব্দ শুনি ও তিনজন যেগে যাই ও চৌকিতে বসি। নাজিম উদ্দিন জিজ্ঞাসা করে কে, বাহির থেকে বলে হাবিব স্যার এসেছে দরজা খুল। নাজিমউদ্দিন সার্ট সায়ে দিয়ে দরজার দিগে যায়। দরজা খুলে হাবিব, দা হাতে ঠান্ডু লাঠি হাতে ঘরে ঢুকে। হাবিব বলে মঞ্জুর সাহেবন স্যার ঘরে তিনজন লোক। মঞ্জুর কাদের বলে যে, পিটাইয়া বের কর। আমরা বের হতে না চাইলে মৃত্যুভয় দেখাইয়া বের করে। বাহির হয়ে দেখি মঞ্জুর কাদের, কেফায়তুল, তরুন, কুবের সহ ৭০/৮০ জন লোক। আমরা পূর্বদিকে যাই। ছাপড়ামত জায়গায় আশ্রয় নেই। মঞ্জুর কাদের শাবল হাতে ঘরে আঘাত করে ও অন্যান্য লোক দরজা বেড়া, টিন ভাঙ্গিয়া লইয়া যায় ও নাঃ জমি খালি পড়িয়া থাকে।” He testified that the men of the defendants ousted them from the house and dismantled and removed the structures of the plaintiff from the suit land. On perusal of the evidence of PWs.2-4 we find that all of them were eye witnesses to the occurrence of dispossession and they, in corroboration with each other, testified as to how and in what manner the defendants evicted the plaintiff from the suit land at night by force. PW.5 Abdus Satter was owner of adjoining land to the suit land and he appears to be a competent and dependable to testify about possession of the suit land. He stated in his evidence “নাঃ জমিতে বাদী ওয়ালী আহমেদ জমি মাটি ভরাট করে। বাদী ওয়ালী মুল বাশের বেড়া দ্বারা একটা ঘর করে। সীমানা চতুর দিকে মুলি বাশের বেড়া করে। বাদীর লোকজন ঐ বাড়ীতে আসত। নাঃ জমি মঞ্জুর কাদের দখল করে এবং টিন সেড ঘর করে জুতার ফ্যাক্টরী করিয়াছে।” he further stated in his examination-in-chief 1991/সনের ৪ঠা নভেম্বর বিবাদী নালিশী জমির দখল নেন। আমি গিয়া দেখি যে, বাদির ঘর দরজা নাই।” Testifying previous possession of the plaintiff, he said that he offered prayer in front of the plaintiffs hit. His evidence along with the testimony of PWs.2-4 has satisfactorily proved the plaintiffs case of possession an dispossession. 

16. DW.I, A.K.M. Hasinul Haque was examined as sole witness of the defendants opposite party, who stated in his examination -in-chief “আমি অত্র মামলায় মঞ্জুর কাদের এর পক্ষে ক্ষমতা পত্র নিয়ে সাক্ষী দিচ্ছি যে, আমার বাসস্থান ধানমন্ডি ১৯ নম্বরে। ০৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে আমি রাত ৩ টার সময় বাসায় ছিলাম। নালিশী জমিতে ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে রাত ৩ টায় কি ঘটে তা আমি দেখিনি।”

17. Defendants have no witness to give testimony in proof of their entering into possession of the suit land against the evidence of PWs. 

18. On perusal of pleadings of the patties, exhibits and evidence on record with regard to the acquisition of title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land we find that Professor Nurun Nahar Ahmed on 01.11.1982 by two registered sale deeds No.3821 and 3822 sold suit land measuring .1650 decimals of land to the plaintiff petitioner and handed over the possession therein with specified boundary given in the schedule of the kabals. After purchase in 1982, plaintiff mutated his name in the khatian and paid rent. At the time of purchase, the suit land was low lying area and the purchaser plaintiff cultivated boro paddy through borgadar and developed the land by earth filing spending money; and the plaintiff demarcated boundary of the suit land by bamboo pillar and bamboo fencing, erected one but with bamboo pillar, bamboo fencing and with tin roof and appointed one caretaker PW. Nizamuddin who used to reside therein to look after the suit land. Plaintiff PW.1 stated in his deposition .“নামজারীর খতিয়ানও দিয়াছি (প্রঃ-৩) ন! ৯৪/২, এসএ খতিয়ান ------ উক্ত প্রকারে আমরা ১৬৫০ শতাংশ ভোগ দখলে আছি। নামজারী করেছি। এই সেই নামজারী খতিয়ান নং-৫৪/৩ (প্রঃ-৬)। কতিপয় খাজনার দাখিলা ডিসিআর দিয়েছি (প্রঃ-৭ সিরিজ) আমি নাঃ জমিতে মাটি ভরাট করেছি। ৩ লক্ষ টাকার কাচাঁ স্লিপ দিয়েছি।” Rent receipts and records of right though not documents of title, are important documentary evidence of possession. In support of this contention, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the case of Erfan Ali Vs. Joynal Abedin Mia (late) represented by his legal heirs Golenur and others, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216. The defendant opposite parties could not controvert the plaintiffs documents Exhibit 3, 6 and 7 series. Defendants purchased land has been mutated in their names separately indicating that their land is not the suit land of this suit. Because two khatians cannot be opened for the same area of land. Moreover, it is evident that the plaintiff purchased the suit land before the purchase by the defendants. It is not acceptable contention that after purchase of the suit land in 1982 and getting name of plaintiff mutated, he would remain silent without taking possession in the suit land. Rather after execution of purchase deed of defendants. Problem cropped up G.D. Entry and complaint case are supporting events in proof of eviction of the plaintiff on 04.11.1991 at 03.00.A.M. 

19. On perusal of the trial Court's judgment, it appears that the trial Court found “বাদী ৯৪/২নং খতিয়ানে তাহার নামে নামজারী পর্চা এবং ডিসিআর ও নালিশী ভূমিতে তাহার দখল সংক্রান্ত তহশীল অফিস কর্তৃক দাখিলী প্রতিবেদন প্রমাণে ব্যবহার করে নাই। But on perusal of the evidence of PW.1, we find it otherwise. All those documents are admitted in evidence as Exhibits 3 and 7 series. These are public documents and need not be proved formally. Again learned Judge found “পিডব্লিউ-১ তাহার জবানবন্দিতে ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিথে রাত্রি অনুমান ৩ টার দিকে নালিশী ভূমিতে বাদীর কেয়ার টেকারকে উচ্ছেদ করিয়া তথায় বাশের খুটিসহ টিনের ঘর ভাংগিয়া ফেলে। জবানবন্দির উক্ত বক্তব্য বাদীর আরজীতে কোথাও বর্ণনা করেন নাই।” On perusal of the plaint, we find in the plaint   “বাশের খুটি ও মুলি বাশের বেড়া ও উপরে টিনের ছাউনি দিয়া গৃহ নির্মান করিয়া তাহাতে একজন কেয়ারটেকার বসাইয়া তাহার সম্পত্তি ভোগ দখল ও রক্ষনাবেক্ষণ করিতে থাকে। ------ বিগত ৪/১১/৯১ ইং তারিখে বহু লোকজন সহকারে দলবদ্ধ হইয়া বল প্রয়োগে বিবাদীগণ বাদীর দখলীয় উক্ত ১৬৫০ শতাংশ ভূমি চারিদিকের বেড়া ও ঘর ভাংগিয়া সরাইয়া ফেলিয়া তাহা বজর দখল করে।” Again the learned Judge found (PW.2) “তিনি জবানবন্দিতে চারিদিকে বাশের বাউন্ডারী ছিল না বলিয়া উল্লেখ করেন।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.2 we find the statement “চারিদিকে বাশের বাউন্ডারী ছিল” The trial Court again found “(পিডব্লিউ-৩) তিনি নালিশী  জমির দক্ষিণে নালা বলিয়া উল্লেখ করেন এবং তাহার দক্ষিণে রাস্তা বলিয়া উল্লেখ করেন। but on perusal of the evidence of PW.3 we find   “দক্ষিণে নালা, তার দক্ষিনে বিল।” The learned Judge of the trial Court found (PW.3) “তিনি নালিশী জমির পূর্বে আঃ সাত্তার বশির উদ্দিন উল্লেখ করেন।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.3 we find “পূর্বে আঃ সাত্তার” and in cross PW.3 stated “পূর্বে আঃ সাত্তার” Again learned Judge found (PW.3) “তিনি কন্ট্রাক্টরের কথা বলিতে বলিতে পারেন নাই।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.3 we find “আমার নেতৃত্বে মাটি ভরাট হয়, বয়লামপুর থেকে মাটি এনে ভরাট করি” and in cross examination “ইহা সত্য নয় যে, মাটি ভরাট করি নাই ও কন্ট্রাক্টর দেই নাই।” Again the trial Court found in his judgment PW.4 said “তিনি তাহার জবানবন্দিতে পূর্ব দিকে ছাপড়ায় আশ্রয় নেন মর্মে উল্লেখ করেন যাহা অন্যান্য সাক্ষীদের সাথে বক্তব্যের মিল পাওয়া যায় না।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.4 we find “আমরা পূর্ব দিকে যাই। ছাপড়া মত জায়গায় আশ্রয় নেই। PW.2 stated in his deposition “আমরা পূর্ব দিকে ৫০/৬০ হাত দূরে আশ্রয় নেই। PW.3 also stated in his deposition “আমরা ৫০/৬০ হাত দূরে পূর্ব দিকে আশ্রয় নেই। Again the trial Court found in his judgment “(পিডব্লিউ ৫) তিনি নালিশী জমির বাউন্ডারী হওয়ার কথা বলিতে পারেন নাই।” but on perusal of the evidence of PW.5 we find “নালিশী জমিতে বাদী আহম্মদ মাটি ভরাট করে। বাদী ওয়ালী মুলি বাশের বেড়া দ্বারা একটা ঘর করে। সীমানা চুতর্দিতে মুলি বাশের বেড়া করে।” Again he found in his judgment “তিনি মঞ্জুর কাদের নালিশী জমিতে নীচু জমি ভরাট সমান করেন মর্মে উল্লেখ করেন।  but on perusal of the evidence of PW.5 we find “নালিশী জমিতে বাদী ওয়ালী আহম্মদ মাটি ভরাট করে।” On scrutiny of the impugned judgment, we therefore, find the above quoted examples of misreading, non-consideration of the pleadings and evidence on record and the learned trial Judge has committed error of law resulting error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and miscarriage of justice. As such, he said judgment calls for our interference. 

20. From the aforesaid discussion of evidence and other facts and circumstances of this case, we hold the view that the plaintiff-petitioner has successfully proved his prior possession and subsequent dispossession by the defendant on 4/11/191 at 3.00 a.m. and immediately after the dispossession, he lodged General Diary No.191 dated 4.11.1991 with the Mohammadpur Police Station and also filed Complaint Case No.1287a-1/91 and thereafter this suit was filed within 6 months on 29.04.1992. But the learned Judge of the Court below could not adjudicate the whole matters in its true perspective, and arrived at a wrong decision in dismissing the suit occasioning failure of justice. When the defendants had taken force able possession without lawful authority and the suit was filed within 6(six) months, it is incumbent upon the Court to restore possession of the plaintiff in the suit land in accordance with boundary demarcation specified in the schedule of the plaint. The defendants may file proper suit to get their legitimate share partitioned, but they cannot be allowed to take law in their hand. 

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissing the suit is set aside and the suit is decreed with costs. The defendant opposite parties are directed to surrender vacant possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner within 60(sixty) days from this date, failing which, the plaintiff-petitioner shall get possession in the suit land restored through the Court by removing the structures therefrom, if any. 

22. Send down the lower Court's record along with a copy of the judgment to the Courts below immediately.

End.
